caption: What if lightning struck you? Lightning hits somewhere on Earth about 44 times every second. An average bolt carries about 300 million volts and 30,000 amps, in a blink. Direct hits are rare: most people are hurt by current spreading through the ground. About 9 in 10 people struck survive, but the heart can stop. Victims carry no charge, so they are safe to touch: call for help and start CPR. Some survivors get red, fern-shaped Lichtenberg marks that fade within a day or two. In India, lightning killed 2,558 people in 2023 (NCRB), about 4 in 10 deaths from natural forces. The free Damini app from IITM Pune alerts you when lightning is within 20 to 40 km. When thunder roars, go indoors, and stay away from open fields, lone trees and water. Plot twist: a hard-top car is safe, but not because of rubber tyres. Its metal body carries the current around you. Did YOU know the car fact? 👇
